subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Definition, log laws, change of base, common vs natural log, problem-solving

questions.stem: If log₂ 8 = x, then x equals:
questions.explanation: Definition of log: log_b(N) = x ⟺ b^x = N. Here log₂ 8 = x ⟺ 2^x = 8 = 2³ → x = 3. Logarithms exist only for POSITIVE arguments (N > 0); the base b > 0 and b ≠ 1. log_b(b) = 1; log_b(1) = 0 for any valid base.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: log(MN) = log M + log N is the:
questions.explanation: Three core log laws: PRODUCT log(MN) = log M + log N; QUOTIENT log(M/N) = log M − log N; POWER log(Mⁿ) = n · log M. These convert multiplications into additions — the original utility of logarithms before calculators (slide rule, log tables). Change of base: log_b X = log_a X / log_a b. Common base 10: just 'log'. Natural log base e ≈ 2.71828: 'ln'.

questions.explanation: Apply product rule: log 25 + log 4 = log(25 × 4) = log 100. Since base is 10: log₁₀ 100 = 2 (because 10² = 100). Always be alert to opportunities to combine log terms — combined arguments often simplify to a power of the base.

questions.stem: If log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, the value of log₁₀ 5 is:
questions.explanation: Use 5 = 10/2. So log 5 = log 10 − log 2 = 1 − 0.3010 = 0.6990. Other handy log identities (base 10): log 3 ≈ 0.4771; log 7 ≈ 0.8451; log 11 ≈ 1.0414; log 2 + log 5 = log 10 = 1 (always).

questions.stem: If 3^x = 81, then the value of x using logarithms is:
questions.explanation: Take log of both sides: x · log 3 = log 81 = log(3⁴) = 4·log 3 → x = 4. Or directly: 81 = 3⁴ so 3^x = 3⁴ → x = 4. Both routes give the same answer; the log method becomes essential when bases don't match nicely (e.g., 3^x = 50).

questions.explanation: Logarithm of a positive number = characteristic (integer part) + mantissa (decimal part). For numbers ≥ 1, characteristic = (digits before decimal point) − 1. 1234 has 4 digits → characteristic = 3. log 1234 ≈ 3.0913, so characteristic 3, mantissa 0.0913. For numbers between 0 and 1, characteristic is negative — written as bar (e.g., log 0.123 ≈ −0.9101, written 1̄.0899).

questions.explanation: Combine using product rule: log₂[x(x−6)] = 4 → x(x−6) = 2⁴ = 16 → x² − 6x − 16 = 0. Quadratic: x = [6 ± √(36 + 64)]/2 = [6 ± 10]/2. x = 8 or x = −2. Reject x = −2 because log of a negative number is undefined (also requires x − 6 > 0, so x > 6). Thus x = 8. Verify: log₂ 8 + log₂ 2 = 3 + 1 = 4 ✓.
